name: Brian Acton
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Computer engineer Brian Acton cofounded messaging app WhatsApp with Jan Koum in 2007; the two had met while working at Yahoo.
The pair sold WhatsApp to Facebook for $22 billion in cash and stock in 2014. Acton left WhatsApp at the end of 2017.
Acton received about $3 billion for his stake in WhatsApp. The mobile messaging app has over 3 billion users in 180 countries.
In 2018, he committed $50 million to Signal Foundation - the nonprofit behind the signal mobile app focused on preserving private communication.
Acton and wife, Tegan, have also founded three other philanthropic entities. In total, the couple holds over $1 billion in charitable vehicles.
forbes_facts: Five years before Facebook bought WhatsApp, Acton had applied for a job at Facebook and was rejected.
Acton tweeted "#deletefacebook" in March 2018 in the wake of revelations that Facebook had enabled Cambridge Analytica to improperly handle data from users.

name: Jack Cockwell
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: A South African native and trained accountant, Jack Cockwell is a famed dealmaker in Canada.
From the 1970s through the early 1990s he built the Bronfmans' Edper conglomerate, acquiring massive holdings in real estate, forestry and mining.
Now known as Brookfield Asset Management, one of the world's biggest money managers, he handed the reins to fellow billionaire Bruce Flatt in 2002.
His wealth comes from a large holding in Brookfield shares, much of it in a partnership shared with other board directors and management.
Cockwell is a member of Ryerson University's board of governors and governor of the Royal Ontario Museum.

name: Tung Chee Hwa
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025)
forbes_bio: Tung Chee Hwa is the eldest son of shipping magnate Tung Chao Yung, who founded what became one of Hong Kong's largest shipping companies.
After running Orient Overseas for 14 years, Chee Hwa handed over the reins to younger brother Chee Chen in order to serve as Hong Kong's first chief executive.
In 2018 the two brothers sold their entire 68.7% stake to China shipping giant COSCO, pocketing $4.3 billion.
His two sons, Alan and Andrew, were both executives at Orient Overseas.

name: Augusto Perfetti
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Augusto Perfetti and his brother Giorgio Perfetti own candy and gum giant Perfetti Van Melle, a company with more than $4.8 billion in revenues in 2024.
Their father Ambrogio and uncle Egidio started the company in 1946 as a chewing gum business in a small town near Milan.
In 2022, the company announced it would acquire Mondelez International's developed market gum business, adding brands such as Trident, Dentyne and Bubbalicious.
Augusto Perfetti named his yacht and his private jet after Mentos mints and Airheads taffy, the company's top-selling brands.
Perfetti once sold a 300-foot yacht under construction to fellow billionaire Suleiman Kerimov.
forbes_facts: Perfetti's father and uncle were inspired to start the company after seeing American soldiers bring gum to Europe during World War II.

name: Don Levin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Don Levin made a fortune in tobacco rolling paper.
Levin's D.R.L. Enterprises owns Republic Brands and a group of companies that owns a paper mill, a rolling paper manufacturing facility and iconic brands including E-Z Wider, OCB and JOB.
Born to a used car salesman, Levin was planning to be a car salesman himself until a friend convinced him to buy a head shop in Chicago named Adams Apple.
Most of the store's customers came in looking for rolling papers, so Levin started a distribution company that sold rolling papers to smoke shops.
In 2000, Levin bought iconic brands OCB and JOB from French paper magnate Vincent Bolloré.
Today Republic does more than $600 million in estimated annual revenue and is one of the biggest players in the rolling paper industry.

name: Caroline Hagen Kjos
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2025)
forbes_bio: Caroline Hagen Kjos became chairman of her family's Canica AS holding company in 2014.
The Swiss resident also received a majority stake in Canica at at that time.
Her father, Norwegian billionaire Stein Erik Hagen, founded discount supermarket Rimi with his father in the 1970s.
Rimi merged with Sweden's ICA group in 1998 and later with Dutch retailer Ahold; Hagen eventually sold his stake, forming Canica AS with the proceeds.
Canica AS now has a number of investments across Scandinavia, including consumer goods manufacturer Orkla ASA and hardware store chain Jernia.
forbes_facts: Caroline has a bachelor's degree in business administration from the Parsons School of Design in New York.

name: Manuel Puig Rocha
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Manuel Puig Rocha is the largest individual shareholder of Puig Brands, a fashion and beauty conglomerate which owns Nina Ricci, Carolina Herrera and Charlotte Tilbury.
The company was founded by his grandfather Antonio Puig in 1914, who got his big break with the Milady Lipstick in 1922.
Rocha has been vice president of Puig Brands since 2007, responsible for overseeing its international subsidiaries.
Rocha's father, Antonio, along with his three uncles Mariano, José María and Enrique joined the company in 1950 and helped bolster its growth.
Today at least 14 family members control Puig Brands.

name: Haluk Bayraktar
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Haluk Bayraktar owns 47.5% of Turkish unmanned military drone manufacturer Baykar. He co-owns it with his brother Selçuk and serves as the CEO.
The company was founded by his father Özdemir in 1984 to make parts for the Turkish auto industry and began making unmanned aerial vehicles in the 2000s.
Baykar recorded sales of $1.9 billion in 2023 and its exports rose to $1.8 billion in 2024, thanks to contracts with militaries in Europe, Africa and the Middle East.
Baykar's most famous export, the Bayraktar drone, has been used so successfully by Ukrainian troops that it inspired a popular folk song.

name: Pavan Jain
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2023-2025)
forbes_bio: Pavan Jain is the chairman of Delhi-based INOX Group.
His son Siddharth Jain  runs INOX Air Products, which supplies medical oxygen, and INOXCVA, which manufactures cryogenic tanks.
His brother Vivek Jain is chairman of the Inox GFL group, which includes listed Gujarat Fluorochemicals and Inox Wind.
In 2023, his INOX Leisure multiplex chain merged with PVR to form India's largest multiplex operator PVR-INOX.
He listed cyrogenics cylinder maker Inox India in 2023 at a 44% premium to the IPO price.
forbes_facts: Patriarch Devendra Jain divided the family's assets in INOX Group in 2021 between Pavan and Vivek.

name: Leonard Abess
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio:
Leonard Abess made headlines for gifting $60 million to more than 450 current and former employees of his City National Bank of Florida after selling it for more than $1 billion during
the financial crisis.

His father, Leonard Abess Sr., cofounded the bank in 1946, but sold it in the 1980s. Abess bought it out of bankruptcy a few years later and grew it to nearly $3 billion in
assets.
Since selling the bank, Abess has bought up nearly 4,000 acres of land across Miami and Vermont, some of which he's using to grow limes.
His company, ThinkLab Ventures, provides capital and financing for commercial real estate development projects.
It also owns a stake in Jersey Jack Pinball, a leading maker of ?artisanal pinball machines? and previously owned a private jet center near Miami.
forbes_facts: Abess bought Sylvester Stallone's former Miami home for $16.2 million in 1999.
Abess is on the board of trustees of the University of Miami.

name: Ulrike Baro
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Ulrike Baro is one of the three daughters of Horst Sartorius, who passed on a 50% stake in biopharmaceutical firm Sartorius AG after his death in 1998.
Her great-grandfather Florenz Sartorius founded the firm in 1870 to make analytical balances to measure small mass in laboratories.
Sartorius AG, which went public in 1990, makes pharmaceutical and laboratory equipment.
Today, the company has around 10,600 employees and annual revenue exceeding $2.5 billion.
forbes_facts: Ulrike shares in the legacy with sisters Karin Herbst-Sartorius, Christine Franken and Christine's sons, Andreas and Kai Christian.
An executor oversees their inheritance until 2028.

name: Joel Glazer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Joel Glazer and his five siblings sold a quarter of their 68% stake in Manchester United to British chemicals billionaire Jim Ratcliffe in 2023.
The deal valued the team at $5.4 billion (net of debt). Their father, shopping mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), bought the team for $1.4 billion in 2005.
The Glazer siblings still own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers; their father acquired the franchise for $192 million in 1995, and it's now worth an estimated $5.2 billion (net of debt).
Joel Glazer co-chairs Man U with his brother Avram and the Bucs with his brothers Bryan and Edward. Another brother, Kevin, runs the family's real estate arm, Glazer Properties.
Sister Darcie Glazer Kassewitz is chairman of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Foundation and two other family charitable foundations.

name: Sergey Lomakin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Sergey Lomakin cofounded Russian discount retailer Fix Price in 2007 together with Artem Khachatryan.
The chain has opened more than 4,000 stores in Russia, Kazakhstan, Georgia, Belarus, Latvia, Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.
Lomakin serves as chairman of the company, which went public in 2021.
His cofounder, Khachatryan, is also a billionaire.
In December 2023 Lomakin bought nearly all of Khachatryan's stake in company for $990 million.
